case_source: (From the judgment and decree dated the 25th day of July, 2016 passed by the High Court Division in F.M.A.No.217 of 2015)
full_judgment:
Abu Bakar Siddiquee J. This civil petition for leave to appeal is directed against the judgment and decree dated the 25th day of July, 2016 passed by the High Court Division in F.M.A.No.217 of 2015 allowing the appeal.

2. The facts, relevant for disposal of this petition, are that the petitioner as plaintiff filed the Title Suit No.994 of 2012 in the Court of 2nd Joint District Judge, Dhaka alleging, inter alia, that the suit property along with some other non-suited property belongs to Dilbar Pramanik, Out of 21.95 acres land, only 17.21 acres land was purchased by Khetra Mohan Paul and Taherun Nessa on 22.09.1932 by an auction sale through Court. Taherun Nessa exhausted her share of the suit property by selling it to others. The plaintiff purchased the suit land from different person in between 1974-1991 and that it got right, title, interest and possession on the suit land. The defendants having no right, title and interest in the suit property claim title therein which compelled them to institute the suit.

3. The plaintiff filed an application for injunction under Order XXXIX, rules 1 and 2 read with section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure for restraining defendant No.1 from disturbing or dispossessing him from his peaceful possession of the suit property.

4. The respondents as defendants contested the aforesaid application by filing written objection contending, inter alia, that the suit property along with other properties were sold in Rent Execution Case No.269 of 1.932. Taherun Nessa and Khetra Mohan and others partitioned their land among themselves and 7.97 acres land of Plot No.522 fell in saham of Khetra Mohan and the land of Plot No.520 along with the land of other plots fell in the saham of Taherun Nessa Bebi and accordingly, S.A. Khatian No.49 was correctly prepared in their names. 2.92 acres land of C.S. Plot No.522 was acquired by the Government for the construction of Dhaka Aricha Road through L.A. Case No.39/51-52 and that while rest 5.05 acres land of C.S. Plot No.522 remained in possession of Khetra Mohan Paul and others, they transferred the said land to Chan Miah through Registered Sub-kabala Deed dated 20.04.1962 and delivered possession to them. Thereafter, Chan Miah transferred 3.29 acres land to Korpula Bibi by Registered Deed No.329 dated 10.01.1963. While Taherun Nessa and Chan Miah had been in possession of their land of C.S. Plot No.520, they transferred 7.73 acres land to Abdur Rob and others vide Registered Deed No.431 dated 16.01.1993. Korpula Bibi transferred 2.31 acres land to Alhaj Sekender Khan through Registered Sub-kabala Deed Nos.3498, 3499, 3500 and 3502. Korpula Bibi on 25.05.1963 further transferred 0.98 acre land to Mrs. Momtaz Akter Kashem through Deed No.3501. Chan Miah transferred her rest 1.76 acres land to Alhaj Sekander Khan on 24.04.1963 through two Registered Deed Nos.4777 and 4778 and delivered possession of the same to the purchaser. Thereafter, Momataz Akter Kashem transferred 0.98 acre land through a sab-kabala Deed being No.4256 to defendant No.1, A.K.M. Jahangir Khan. The land of CS and SA Plot No.522 was recorded in the name of defendant No.1 and his father, Sekander Khan measuring 0.98 and 4.07 acres respectively and that in R.S.Khatian No.221, the said record of rights was correctly prepared in his name. Thereafter, Alhaj Sakender Khan died leaving behind his wife-Mrs. Tahera Khatun, one son, AKM Jahangir Khan. (the defendant) and four daughters who got their names mutated and they had been in possession of the same one payment of the rents to the Government. Taharun Nessa, wife of Sakender Khan, gifted her property in favour of her four daughters and thereafter passed away leaving son and daughters. Momtaz Begum, daughter of Sakender Khan thereafter expired leaving behind her husband, two daughters and three sisters. Out of 4.07 acres land of late Sekander Khan, defendant No.1, AKM Jahangir Khan, got 1.19 acres land and he also purchased 0.98 acre land from Momtaz Akther through sub-kabala Deed No.4256 dated 11.07.1963 and thus, he acquired 2.17 acres land. Defendant No.1 filed Title Suit No.5733 of 2008 in the Court of Joint District Judge, 6th Court, Dhaka against the co-sharers for partition of their ejmali land and on 25.05.2009, the said suit was decreed on compromise. As per the said decree, 2.17 acres land fell in the saham of defendant No.1 who mutated his name and had been in possession of the said land and had been paying rents regularly to the Government. During B.S. Survey, 2.17 acres land was recorded in the name of defendant No.1 in Plot No.4707 in Khatian No.968 in the field porcha, defendant No.1 constructed a boundary wall on four sides of his 2.17 acres land and constructed three pucca houses therein and he has been in possession of the same by appointing caretaker. Defendant Nos.1-6 previously instituted Title Suit No.325 of 1981 and in the said suit, the plaintiff was impleaded as defendant No.13 and the said suit was decreed in favour of the present defendants. The plaintiffs along with some other miscreants on 03.11.2011 demolished the defendants boundary wall and also constructed semi-pucca houses constructed thereon. The application for injunction is based on a false story and the same is liable to be rejected.

5. The learned Joint District Judge after hearing the parties by the judgment and order dated 27.01.2013 granted injunction restraining defendant No.1 from disturbing the peaceful possession of the plaintiff in the suit property. 6. Being aggrieved by the judgment and decree of the trial Court, the defendant preferred First Miscellaneous Appeal (FMA) No.217 of 2015 before the High Court Division, and the High Court Division after hearing the appeal allowed the same reversing the judgment and order dated 27.01.2013 of the learned Joint District Judge, 2nd Court, Dhaka in Title Suit No.994 of 2012; hence, this petition for leave to appeal.

7. Mr. Md. Ali Reza, learned Advocate, appearing for the petitioner, submits that the High Court Division failed to conceive the points raised in the arguments of the learned Advocate for the plaintiff-respondent appellant in Miscellaneous Appeal No.217 of 2015 and failed to discuss the same in the judgment. He further submits that the High Court Division committed an error of law in considering the facts and legal aspect of the appeal and arbitrarily allowed the appeal setting aside the judgment and order dated 27.01.2013 of the trial Court. He also submits that the High Court Division failed to consider that order No.4 dated 22.04.2010 of Title Execution Case No.5 of 2006 is still valid since the decree-holder, namely, the appellant did not challenge the same in any higher Court and as such, the judgment and order is liable to be set aside. He again submits that the plaintiff filed Title Suit No. 994 of 2012 for declaration about the suit property and the plaintiff stated in his plaint that the defendants had been never in possession of the suit property within the same boundary, the plaintiff would prove the same by producing evidence and that the High Court Division ought to have considered the matter and as such, the judgment and order is liable to be set aside. He further submits that the High Court Division failed to consider that the decree in Title Suit No.325 of 1982 for permanent injunction and the respondent stated in his written objection and written statement that the plaintiff violated the decree and as such, they filed Execution Case No.05 of 2006 and on this aspect, the decree cannot sustain in law and as such, the judgment and order is liable to be set aside.

8. Mr. Quarnrul Hoque Siddique, learned Counsel, appearing for respondent No.1, AKM Jahangir Khan, in his submissions, supported the impugned judgment and order of the High Court Division. He contends that this respondent and others as plaintiff previously instituted Title Suit No.325 of 1981 against the present petitioner and others for permanent injunction and the suit was decreed in favour of the present respondents on being satisfied that they are in possession of the suit property and in the present suit, i.e. Suit No.994 of 2012 the learned Joint District Judge illegally granted injunction restraining the present respondent not to disturb the present petitioner in the suit property which is against the principle of law. He also submits that the present petitioner has got no possession in the suit property and by misrepresenting the facts of the case have obtained the injunction which is not sustainable in law.

9. We have heard the learned Advocates for both the parties, perused the materials on record.

10. It is admitted that Title Suit No.325 of 1981 and Title Suit No.5733 of 2008 were disposed of in between the parties. The learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the defendant-appellant vehemently argued the aforesaid fact of institution of more than one suit earlier operates res judicata and as such, the present Title Suit No.994 of 2012 is not maintainable in its present form. He further submits that no interim injunction can be granted when the suit is found prima facie barred res judicata. It is true that previously when in previous litigations, it is found that the defendant-appellant is the true owner in possession of the property, it is difficult to make an order of equitable relief like injunction.

11. The present defendant-respondent and his other co-sharers (present defendant Nos. 1-6) as plaintiffs instituted Title Suit No.325 of 1981 before the then Sub-ordinate Judge, 2" Court, Dhaka impleading the present plaintiff (as defendant No.13) and others for permanent injunction in respect of 5.05 acres land of C.S Khatian No.32 and C.S and S.A Plot No.522 corresponding to R.S. Khatian No.221 and R.S Plot No.1127. The suit was contested by defendant Nos.7 and 13 (present plaintiff) and the learned Sub-ordinate Judge by his judgment and decree dated 01.03.2001 decreed the suit restraining the present plaintiff from dispossessing or disturbing the plaintiffs of that suit from their peaceful possession of the suit property. The present plaintiff did not move the higher Court against the said judgment and decree with a view to challenge the said decree. Thereafter, defendant No.13 of the aforementioned suit, as plain-tiff, instituted present Title Suit No.994of 2012 impleading the present defendants (plaintiff of the previous suit as defendant Nos.1-6) and prayed for declaration of his title in the suit property and for further declaration that 5.05 acres land of R.S Plot No.1127 of R.S. khatian No. 221 published in the name of Alhaj Sekander Khan is wrong and that the name of the predecessor of the present plaintiff wrongly has been omitted and that the title deeds of the plain-tiff in respect of Kha scheduled land are false, forged and collusive and not binding upon the plaintiff only. In the present suit, the plaintiff-petitioner claims title over 2.56 acres land out of 5.05 acres land of C.S and S.A. Plot No.522 corresponding to R.S. Khatian No.221 and R.S. Plot No.1127. The learned Advocate for the defendant-respondent raised objection to the claim of the plaintiff-petitioner and submitted that the present defendant-respondent claims title over 1.17 acres land out of 5.05 acres land and the rest land of the CS Plot No.522 is in possession of the present plaintiff. In reply to the said submission, the learned Advocate for the defendant-respondent has submitted that it would be evident from the written objection of the plaintiff-respondent filed against the application for injunction that defendant No.1 had filed Title Suit No.5733 of 2008 in the 6th Court of the learned Joint District Judge, Dhaka against his co-sharers for partition and obtained a compromise decree on 25.05.2009 and as per solenama, this 2.17 acres land out of 5.05 acres land has fallen in the saham of this defendant-respondent and the rest land has fallen in the saham of other co-sharers.

12. From the description of the plaint of the present suit, it appears that the present plaintiff-petitioner has claimed his title over 2.56 acres land out of 5.05 acres land which was the subject matter of the previous Title Suit No.325 of 1981 instituted by the present defendant-respondent and other co-sharers for permanent injunction and obtained decree for permanent injunction against the present plaintiff-respondent on 01.03.2001. Thereafter, this defendant brought an allegation that on 15.02.2006 at 7 P.M., the present plaintiff-petitioner forcibly entered into the suit land and took away house container from the decreetal land through a crane and was trying to dis-possess them from the decreetal land.

13. Jurisdiction of the Court to interfere with an order of interlocutory or temporary injunction is purely equitable and, therefore, the Court being approached, will, apart from other considerations, also to look into the conduct of the party invoking the jurisdiction of the Court, and may refuse to interfere unless his conduct was free from blame. Since the relief is wholly equitable in nature, the party invoking the jurisdiction of the Courts to show that he him-self was not at fault and that he himself was not responsible for bringing about the state of things complained of and that he was not unfair or inequitable in his dealings with the party against whom he was seeking relief. These considerations will arise not only in respect of the person who seeks an order of injunction, but also in respect of the party approaching the Court for vacating the ad-interim or temporary injunction order.

14. The learned Joint District Judge allowed the injunction petition relying on the contents of order dated 22.04.2010 and held that from order dated 22.04.2010 passed in Title Execution Case No.05 of 2006 shows that the suit land is in possession of the present plaintiff-petitioner. On careful examining the order dated 22.04.2010, it appears that the defendant-respondent never admitted that the plaintiff-petitioner on 15.02.2006 dispossessed him from the suit land and that defendant is not in possession of the suit property. The plaintiff-petitioner was restrained by a decree for permanent injunction in Title Suit No.325 of 1981 not to evict the defendant-respondent or to disturb his peaceful possession in the suit land. In such circumstances, the trial Court was not justified in granting injunction holding that the defendant-respondent is not in possession of the suit property. But the learned Judges of the High Court Division is very much justified on reversing the judgment and order passed by the learned Joint District Judge. Thus, there is no scope to interfere with the impugned judgment.

15. Considering the entire facts and circumstances of the case, the jurisdiction of granting injunction being an equitable relief, no injunction should be granted at the instance of the plaintiff-petitioner against the defendant-respondent since he has not come with clean hand. We also hold the view that the learned Judge of the High Court Division refused to extend his hand in granting such judicial discretion and as such, there is nothing to interfere into the matter.

16. We find no merit in this leave petition. Accordingly, the civil petition for leave to appeal is dismissed without any order as to costs.

End.
